156	
157	def verify_prefix_windows(path: str, parts: list[dict]) -> bool:
158	    """Verify the leading byte windows of ``path``; trailing bytes allowed.
159	
160	    A merged segment keeps the size and sha256 of every source segment as
161	    verification material; the merged bytes are the exact concatenation of
162	    those windows, so one streaming read re-checks every source segment. An
163	    active (still growing) segment uses the same check against its preserved
164	    prefix windows.
165	    """
166	    if not parts:
167	        return True
168	    with open(path, "rb") as handle:
169	        for part in parts:
170	            h = hashlib.sha256()
171	            remaining = part["size"]
172	            while remaining:
173	                chunk = handle.read(min(_CHUNK, remaining))
174	                if not chunk:
175	                    return False
176	                h.update(chunk)
177	                remaining -= len(chunk)
178	            if h.hexdigest() != part["sha256"]:
179	                return False
180	    return True

184	    """Resolved view of where the log data, lock and cache live."""

230	@contextlib.contextmanager
231	def file_lock(lock_path: str, *, timeout: Optional[float], shared: bool) -> Iterator[None]:
232	    """Serialize access to one log behind a process-shared OS file lock.
233	
234	    Readers take a shared lock and the writer an exclusive one. The backing
235	    primitive is chosen per platform at call time (``fcntl.flock`` on POSIX,
236	    ``LockFileEx`` on Windows), so this module imports cleanly everywhere.
237	
238	    A timeout that elapses raises ``TimeoutError`` (an ``OSError`` subclass);
239	    permission failures and path-class system errors propagate as their
240	    native ``OSError`` subclasses -- callers signal all of them silently via
241	    exit code two.
242	    """
243	    if sys.platform == "win32":  # pragma: win32 cover
244	        backend = _windows_lock
245	    else:
246	        backend = _posix_lock
247	
248	    fd = os.open(lock_path, os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT, 0o600)
249	    acquired = False
250	    try:
251	        backend(fd, shared=shared, timeout=timeout)
252	        acquired = True
253	        yield
254	    finally:
255	        if acquired:
256	            with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
257	                _unlock(fd)
258	        os.close(fd)

261	def _posix_lock(fd: int, *, shared: bool, timeout: Optional[float]) -> None:
262	    import fcntl
263	
264	    mode = fcntl.LOCK_SH if shared else fcntl.LOCK_EX
265	    if timeout is None:
266	        fcntl.flock(fd, mode)
267	        return
268	    deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
269	    while True:
270	        try:
271	            fcntl.flock(fd, mode | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
272	            return
273	        except BlockingIOError:
274	            if time.monotonic() >= deadline:
275	                raise TimeoutError(f"audit log lock busy: fd {fd}")
276	            time.sleep(_LOCK_POLL_SECONDS)

280	    if sys.platform == "win32":  # pragma: win32 cover
281	        _windows_unlock(fd)
282	    else:
283	        import fcntl
284	
285	        fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)

288	def _windows_lock(fd: int, *, shared: bool, timeout: Optional[float]) -> None:  # pragma: win32 cover
289	    import ctypes
290	    from ctypes import wintypes
291	
292	    import msvcrt
293	
294	    LOCKFILE_EXCLUSIVE_LOCK = 0x00000002
295	    LOCKFILE_FAIL_IMMEDIATELY = 0x00000001
296	    ERROR_LOCK_VIOLATION = 33
297	
298	    class _Overlapped(ctypes.Structure):
299	        _fields_ = [
300	            ("Internal", ctypes.c_void_p),
301	            ("InternalHigh", ctypes.c_void_p),
302	            ("Offset", wintypes.DWORD),
303	            ("OffsetHigh", wintypes.DWORD),
304	            ("hEvent", wintypes.HANDLE),
305	        ]
306	
307	    kernel32 = ctypes.WinDLL("kernel32", use_last_error=True)
308	    lock_file_ex = kernel32.LockFileEx
309	    lock_file_ex.restype = wintypes.BOOL
310	    lock_file_ex.argtypes = [
311	        wintypes.HANDLE,
312	        wintypes.DWORD,
313	        wintypes.DWORD,
314	        wintypes.DWORD,
315	        wintypes.DWORD,
316	        ctypes.POINTER(_Overlapped),
317	    ]
318	
319	    handle = msvcrt.get_osfhandle(fd)
320	    flags = LOCKFILE_FAIL_IMMEDIATELY if timeout is not None else 0
321	    if not shared:
322	        flags |= LOCKFILE_EXCLUSIVE_LOCK
323	    deadline = None if timeout is None else time.monotonic() + timeout
324	    while True:
325	        overlapped = _Overlapped()
326	        if lock_file_ex(handle, flags, 0, 0xFFFFFFFF, 0xFFFFFFFF, ctypes.byref(overlapped)):
327	            return

329	        if error != ERROR_LOCK_VIOLATION:
330	            raise OSError(error, f"LockFileEx failed (error {error})")
331	        if deadline is not None and time.monotonic() >= deadline:
332	            raise TimeoutError(f"audit log lock busy: fd {fd}")

377	class AuditMetadataError(ValueError):
378	    """A tampered manifest or verify cache.
379	
380	    Distinct from a malformed record line: damaged *metadata* is reported as
381	    chain corruption (verify returns ``ok=False``), whereas a half-written
382	    record keeps its existing bad-line semantics (ValueError, exit code 2).
383	    """
384	
385	
386	def default_manifest(first: str) -> dict:
387	    return {
388	        "version": 1,
389	        "active": first,
390	        "segments": [{"name": first, "sealed": False, "parts": []}],
391	    }
392	
393	
394	def _manifest_payload_text(manifest: dict) -> str:
395	    body = {
396	        "version": manifest["version"],
397	        "active": manifest["active"],
398	        "segments": manifest["segments"],
399	    }
400	    # The archive location is part of the signed body only when present, so
401	    # manifests written before two-tier storage existed keep their tags.
402	    if manifest.get("archive") is not None:
403	        body["archive"] = manifest["archive"]
404	    return rec.canonical_json(body)
405	
406	
407	def sign_manifest(manifest: dict) -> dict:
408	    """Return a manifest copy carrying its authentication tag."""
409	    signed = {
410	        "version": manifest["version"],
411	        "active": manifest["active"],
412	        "segments": manifest["segments"],
413	    }
414	    if manifest.get("archive") is not None:
415	        signed["archive"] = manifest["archive"]
416	    signed["tag"] = hashlib.sha256(
417	        _manifest_payload_text(signed).encode(_ENCODING)
418	    ).hexdigest()
419	    return signed
420	
421	
422	def load_manifest(layout: Layout) -> Optional[dict]:
423	    try:
424	        with open(layout.manifest_path, "rb") as handle:
425	            raw = handle.read()
426	    except FileNotFoundError:
427	        return None
428	    try:
429	        manifest = json.loads(raw.decode(_ENCODING))
430	    except (UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError) as exc:
431	        raise AuditMetadataError("malformed audit manifest") from exc
432	    if not isinstance(manifest, dict) or not _valid_manifest(manifest):
433	        raise AuditMetadataError("malformed audit manifest")
434	    tag = manifest.get("tag")
435	    if tag is not None:
436	        if not isinstance(tag, str):
437	            raise AuditMetadataError("tampered audit manifest")
438	        expected = hashlib.sha256(
439	            _manifest_payload_text(manifest).encode(_ENCODING)
440	        ).hexdigest()
441	        if not constant_time_equal(tag, expected):
442	            raise AuditMetadataError("tampered audit manifest")
443	    # A manifest without a tag was written by the pre-tag build: structurally
444	    # valid and accepted read-only; the next write re-signs it.
445	    return manifest
446	
447	
448	def _valid_manifest(manifest: Any) -> bool:
449	    if not isinstance(manifest, dict):
450	        return False
451	    if manifest.get("version") != 1 or not isinstance(manifest.get("active"), str):
452	        return False
453	    archive = manifest.get("archive")
454	    if archive is not None and not isinstance(archive, str):
455	        return False
456	    segments = manifest.get("segments")
457	    if not isinstance(segments, list) or not segments:
458	        return False
459	    for index, segment in enumerate(segments):
460	        if not isinstance(segment, dict):
461	            return False
462	        if not isinstance(segment.get("name"), str) or not isinstance(
463	            segment.get("sealed"), bool
464	        ):
465	            return False
466	        archived = segment.get("archived", False)
467	        if not isinstance(archived, bool):
468	            return False
469	        if archived:
470	            # An archived segment lives in the recorded archive location; it
471	            # is always sealed and never the active segment.
472	            if not archive or not segment["sealed"]:
473	                return False
474	            if segment["name"] == manifest["active"]:
475	                return False
476	        parts = segment.get("parts")
477	        if not isinstance(parts, list):
478	            return False
479	        for part in parts:
480	            if not _valid_part(part):
481	                return False
482	        if index == len(segments) - 1:
483	            if segment["name"] != manifest["active"] or segment["sealed"]:
484	                return False
485	        elif not segment["sealed"] or not parts:
486	            return False
487	    tag = manifest.get("tag")
488	    if tag is not None and not isinstance(tag, str):
489	        return False
490	    return True
491	
492	
493	def _valid_part(part: Any) -> bool:
494	    return (
495	        isinstance(part, dict)
496	        and isinstance(part.get("name"), str)
497	        and isinstance(part.get("size"), int)
498	        and isinstance(part.get("sha256"), str)
499	    )
500	
501	
502	def save_manifest(layout: Layout, manifest: dict) -> None:
503	    save_manifest_at(layout.data_dir, manifest)
504	
505	
506	def save_manifest_at(directory: str, manifest: dict) -> None:
507	    """Write a signed manifest into an arbitrary directory (e.g. staging)."""
508	    signed = sign_manifest(manifest)
509	    atomic_write_text(directory, MANIFEST_NAME, rec.canonical_json(signed))
510	
511	
512	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
513	# Incremental verify cache
514	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
515	
516	
517	def cache_tag_payload(version: int, segments: dict) -> bytes:
518	    return rec.canonical_json({"version": version, "segments": segments}).encode(
519	        _ENCODING
520	    )
521	
522	
523	def load_cache(layout: Layout) -> Optional[dict]:
524	    """Load the verify cache or return None when absent.
525	
526	    A present cache whose authentication tag fails to verify is tampering:
527	    ``AuditMetadataError`` is raised rather than silently rebuilding, because
528	    reporting a clean pass off a forged cache must be impossible.
529	    """
530	    try:
531	        with open(layout.cache_path, "rb") as handle:
532	            raw = handle.read()
533	    except FileNotFoundError:
534	        return None
535	    try:
536	        cache = json.loads(raw.decode(_ENCODING))
537	    except (UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError) as exc:
538	        raise AuditMetadataError("tampered audit cache") from exc
539	    if not isinstance(cache, dict) or cache.get("version") != 1:
540	        raise AuditMetadataError("tampered audit cache")
541	    tag = cache.get("tag")
542	    segments = cache.get("segments")
543	    if not isinstance(tag, str) or not isinstance(segments, dict):
544	        raise AuditMetadataError("tampered audit cache")
545	    expected = hashlib.sha256(cache_tag_payload(1, segments)).hexdigest()
546	    if not constant_time_equal(tag, expected):
547	        raise AuditMetadataError("tampered audit cache")
548	    if not _valid_cache_segments(segments):
549	        raise AuditMetadataError("tampered audit cache")
550	    return {"version": 1, "segments": segments, "tag": tag}
551	
552	
553	def constant_time_equal(actual: str, expected: str) -> bool:
554	    if len(actual) != len(expected):
555	        return False
556	    result = 0
557	    for a, b in zip(actual, expected):
558	        result |= ord(a) ^ ord(b)
559	    return result == 0
560	
561	
562	def _valid_cache_segments(segments: Any) -> bool:
563	    if not isinstance(segments, dict):
564	        return False
565	    for name, entry in segments.items():
566	        if not isinstance(name, str) or not isinstance(entry, dict):
567	            return False
568	        if (
569	            not isinstance(entry.get("records"), int)
570	            or entry["records"] < 0
571	            or not isinstance(entry.get("size"), int)
572	            or entry["size"] < 0
573	            or not isinstance(entry.get("mtime_ns"), int)
574	            or not isinstance(entry.get("ctime_ns"), int)
575	        ):
576	            return False
577	        parts = entry.get("parts")
578	        if not isinstance(parts, list):
579	            return False
580	        for part in parts:
581	            if not _valid_part(part):
582	                return False
583	        # The fold is absent only in a structurally-valid pre-fold cache,
584	        # which the walker rebuilds from bytes; a present but malformed fold
585	        # cannot be trusted and is treated like any forged field.
586	        fold = entry.get("fold")
587	        if fold is not None:
588	            if not isinstance(fold, str) or len(fold) != 64:
589	                return False
590	            try:
591	                int(fold, 16)
592	            except ValueError:
593	                return False
594	        tenants = entry.get("tenants")
595	        if not isinstance(tenants, dict):
596	            return False
597	        for tenant, state in tenants.items():
598	            if not isinstance(tenant, str) or not isinstance(state, list):
599	                return False
600	            if len(state) != 3:
601	                return False
602	            count, digest, bad = state
603	            if (
604	                not isinstance(count, int)
605	                or not isinstance(digest, str)
606	                or not isinstance(bad, int)
607	                or count < 0
608	                or bad < -1
609	            ):
610	                return False
611	    return True
612	
613	
614	def save_cache(layout: Layout, segments: dict) -> None:
615	    tag = hashlib.sha256(cache_tag_payload(1, segments)).hexdigest()
616	    payload = {"version": 1, "segments": segments, "tag": tag}
617	    atomic_write_text(
618	        layout.cache_dir, layout.cache_name, rec.canonical_json(payload)
619	    )

628	    with open(path, "rb") as handle:
629	        return handle.read()

"""File-level storage primitives: layout, locking, manifest and cache.

Two on-disk layouts are supported:

* segment store -- ``path`` is a directory holding ordered segment files
  (``seg-00000001.jsonl`` ...), an atomic ``manifest.json`` and a tamper
  evident verify cache;
* legacy single file -- ``path`` is a plain JSON-lines file, exactly as the
  pre-extension log wrote it. Its verify cache lives next to it as a
  dotfile; ``rotate()`` migrates the file itself into a segment store.

A segment store is optionally two-tiered: the manifest records an archive
directory (the cold tier) and flags the sealed segments that were migrated
there, so every reader resolves a segment's bytes to exactly one of the
two locations.

The lock file is a sibling dotfile (``.<name>.lock``) for *both* layouts, so
migrating a file into a segment store never changes the lock path and a
migration in progress stays mutually exclusive with readers. Locking uses
the native system capability of each platform (``flock`` on POSIX,
``LockFileEx`` on Windows); importing this module never depends on one
platform's primitives.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import contextlib
import hashlib
import itertools
import json
import os
import sys
import time
from typing import Any, Iterator, Optional

from . import record as rec

_ENCODING = "utf-8"
LOCK_SUFFIX = ".lock"
MANIFEST_NAME = "manifest.json"
CACHE_NAME = ".verify-cache"
SEG_PREFIX = "seg-"
SEG_SUFFIX = ".jsonl"
FIRST_SEQ = 1
_CHUNK = 1 << 20
_LOCK_POLL_SECONDS = 0.01
_tmp_counter = itertools.count()


def _tmp_name_for(name: str) -> str:
    # Unique per call so concurrent processes/threads never collide on the
    # staging temp file of one atomic replace.
    return f".{name}.{os.getpid()}.{next(_tmp_counter)}.tmp"

# When set, the process hard-kills itself at the named crash point. Used by
# the crash-injection matrix (real SIGKILL, never an in-process exception).
_CRASH_ENV = "AUDIT_CHAIN_CRASH"


def crash_point(name: str) -> None:
    """Kill this process at ``name`` when the crash-injection hook matches.

    The hook is consumed on match so any forked descendant cannot loop on
    it. The kill is asynchronous and ungraceful: no ``finally`` handlers or
    interpreter cleanup run, exactly like ``kill -9``.
    """
    if os.environ.get(_CRASH_ENV) != name:
        return
    os.environ.pop(_CRASH_ENV, None)
    _hard_exit()


def _hard_exit() -> None:
    import signal

    if sys.platform == "win32":  # pragma: win32 cover
        # There is no SIGKILL on Windows; TerminateProcess semantics are the
        # closest hard kill. os.kill with SIGTERM calls TerminateProcess.
        os.kill(os.getpid(), signal.SIGTERM)
    else:
        os.kill(os.getpid(), signal.SIGKILL)
    # Defense in depth in case the signal is caught/held.
    os._exit(137)


def seg_name(seq: int) -> str:
    return f"{SEG_PREFIX}{seq:08d}{SEG_SUFFIX}"


def seg_seq(name: str) -> Optional[int]:
    if not (name.startswith(SEG_PREFIX) and name.endswith(SEG_SUFFIX)):
        return None
    middle = name[len(SEG_PREFIX) : -len(SEG_SUFFIX)]
    if len(middle) != 8 or not middle.isdigit():
        return None
    return int(middle)


def atomic_write_text(directory: str, name: str, text: str) -> None:
    """Durably replace ``directory/name`` with ``text`` (fsync + rename)."""
    atomic_write_bytes(directory, name, text.encode(_ENCODING))


def atomic_write_bytes(directory: str, name: str, raw: bytes) -> None:
    """Durably replace ``directory/name`` with ``raw`` (fsync + rename)."""
    tmp_path = os.path.join(directory, _tmp_name_for(name))
    try:
        with open(tmp_path, "wb") as handle:
            handle.write(raw)
            handle.flush()
            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
        crash_point(f"atomic:{name}:before_replace")
        os.replace(tmp_path, os.path.join(directory, name))
        crash_point(f"atomic:{name}:after_replace")
        fsync_dir(directory)
    except BaseException:
        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
            os.remove(tmp_path)
        raise


def fsync_dir(directory: str) -> None:
    """Best-effort directory sync; never fails the caller.

    Some environments (notably Windows, where a directory cannot be opened
    as a file handle at all) provide no way to sync a directory. Append and
    recovery must still complete there, so an ``OSError`` from opening or
    syncing the directory is tolerated: the atomic-rename commit protocol
    already keeps every crash window on one complete topology.
    """
    flags = os.O_RDONLY
    if hasattr(os, "O_DIRECTORY"):
        flags |= os.O_DIRECTORY
    try:
        fd = os.open(directory, flags)
    except OSError:
        return
    try:
        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
            os.fsync(fd)
    finally:
        os.close(fd)


def verify_windows(path: str, parts: list[dict]) -> bool:
    """Verify retained byte windows (parts) cover the whole file.

    The file size must equal the windows' total and each window's sha256
    must match. Used for sealed (never-growing) segments.
    """
    actual_size = os.path.getsize(path)
    return actual_size == sum(part["size"] for part in parts) and verify_prefix_windows(
        path, parts
    )


def verify_prefix_windows(path: str, parts: list[dict]) -> bool:
    """Verify the leading byte windows of ``path``; trailing bytes allowed.

    A merged segment keeps the size and sha256 of every source segment as
    verification material; the merged bytes are the exact concatenation of
    those windows, so one streaming read re-checks every source segment. An
    active (still growing) segment uses the same check against its preserved
    prefix windows.
    """
    if not parts:
        return True
    with open(path, "rb") as handle:
        for part in parts:
            h = hashlib.sha256()
            remaining = part["size"]
            while remaining:
                chunk = handle.read(min(_CHUNK, remaining))
                if not chunk:
                    return False
                h.update(chunk)
                remaining -= len(chunk)
            if h.hexdigest() != part["sha256"]:
                return False
    return True


class Layout:
    """Resolved view of where the log data, lock and cache live."""

    def __init__(self, root: str, kind: str):
        self.root = root
        self.kind = kind  # "dir" or "file"
        # The lock is a sibling dotfile in both layouts, so its identity is
        # stable across the file -> segment-store migration.
        normalized = os.path.normpath(root)
        parent = os.path.dirname(normalized) or "."
        self.lock_path = os.path.join(
            parent, "." + os.path.basename(normalized) + LOCK_SUFFIX
        )
        if kind == "dir":
            self.data_dir = root
            self.manifest_path = os.path.join(root, MANIFEST_NAME)
            self.cache_dir = root
            self.cache_name = CACHE_NAME
        else:
            directory = os.path.dirname(root) or "."
            self.data_dir = directory
            self.manifest_path = ""
            self.cache_dir = directory
            self.cache_name = "." + os.path.basename(root) + ".verify-cache"

    @property
    def cache_path(self) -> str:
        return os.path.join(self.cache_dir, self.cache_name)

    def segment_path(self, name: str) -> str:
        return os.path.join(self.data_dir, name)


def resolve_existing(path: str) -> Optional[Layout]:
    """Resolve an existing log path, or return None when nothing is there."""
    if os.path.isdir(path):
        return Layout(path, "dir")
    if os.path.isfile(path):
        return Layout(path, "file")
    return None


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Cross-platform process-shared file locking
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


@contextlib.contextmanager
def file_lock(lock_path: str, *, timeout: Optional[float], shared: bool) -> Iterator[None]:
    """Serialize access to one log behind a process-shared OS file lock.

    Readers take a shared lock and the writer an exclusive one. The backing
    primitive is chosen per platform at call time (``fcntl.flock`` on POSIX,
    ``LockFileEx`` on Windows), so this module imports cleanly everywhere.

    A timeout that elapses raises ``TimeoutError`` (an ``OSError`` subclass);
    permission failures and path-class system errors propagate as their
    native ``OSError`` subclasses -- callers signal all of them silently via
    exit code two.
    """
    if sys.platform == "win32":  # pragma: win32 cover
        backend = _windows_lock
    else:
        backend = _posix_lock

    fd = os.open(lock_path, os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT, 0o600)
    acquired = False
    try:
        backend(fd, shared=shared, timeout=timeout)
        acquired = True
        yield
    finally:
        if acquired:
            with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
                _unlock(fd)
        os.close(fd)


def _posix_lock(fd: int, *, shared: bool, timeout: Optional[float]) -> None:
    import fcntl

    mode = fcntl.LOCK_SH if shared else fcntl.LOCK_EX
    if timeout is None:
        fcntl.flock(fd, mode)
        return
    deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
    while True:
        try:
            fcntl.flock(fd, mode | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
            return
        except BlockingIOError:
            if time.monotonic() >= deadline:
                raise TimeoutError(f"audit log lock busy: fd {fd}")
            time.sleep(_LOCK_POLL_SECONDS)


def _unlock(fd: int) -> None:
    if sys.platform == "win32":  # pragma: win32 cover
        _windows_unlock(fd)
    else:
        import fcntl

        fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)


def _windows_lock(fd: int, *, shared: bool, timeout: Optional[float]) -> None:  # pragma: win32 cover
    import ctypes
    from ctypes import wintypes

    import msvcrt

    LOCKFILE_EXCLUSIVE_LOCK = 0x00000002
    LOCKFILE_FAIL_IMMEDIATELY = 0x00000001
    ERROR_LOCK_VIOLATION = 33

    class _Overlapped(ctypes.Structure):
        _fields_ = [
            ("Internal", ctypes.c_void_p),
            ("InternalHigh", ctypes.c_void_p),
            ("Offset", wintypes.DWORD),
            ("OffsetHigh", wintypes.DWORD),
            ("hEvent", wintypes.HANDLE),
        ]

    kernel32 = ctypes.WinDLL("kernel32", use_last_error=True)
    lock_file_ex = kernel32.LockFileEx
    lock_file_ex.restype = wintypes.BOOL
    lock_file_ex.argtypes = [
        wintypes.HANDLE,
        wintypes.DWORD,
        wintypes.DWORD,
        wintypes.DWORD,
        wintypes.DWORD,
        ctypes.POINTER(_Overlapped),
    ]

    handle = msvcrt.get_osfhandle(fd)
    flags = LOCKFILE_FAIL_IMMEDIATELY if timeout is not None else 0
    if not shared:
        flags |= LOCKFILE_EXCLUSIVE_LOCK
    deadline = None if timeout is None else time.monotonic() + timeout
    while True:
        overlapped = _Overlapped()
        if lock_file_ex(handle, flags, 0, 0xFFFFFFFF, 0xFFFFFFFF, ctypes.byref(overlapped)):
            return
        error = ctypes.get_last_error()
        if error != ERROR_LOCK_VIOLATION:
            raise OSError(error, f"LockFileEx failed (error {error})")
        if deadline is not None and time.monotonic() >= deadline:
            raise TimeoutError(f"audit log lock busy: fd {fd}")
        time.sleep(_LOCK_POLL_SECONDS)


def _windows_unlock(fd: int) -> None:  # pragma: win32 cover
    import ctypes
    from ctypes import wintypes

    import msvcrt

    class _Overlapped(ctypes.Structure):
        _fields_ = [
            ("Internal", ctypes.c_void_p),
            ("InternalHigh", ctypes.c_void_p),
            ("Offset", wintypes.DWORD),
            ("OffsetHigh", wintypes.DWORD),
            ("hEvent", wintypes.HANDLE),
        ]

    kernel32 = ctypes.WinDLL("kernel32", use_last_error=True)
    unlock_file_ex = kernel32.UnlockFileEx
    unlock_file_ex.argtypes = [
        wintypes.HANDLE,
        wintypes.DWORD,
        wintypes.DWORD,
        wintypes.DWORD,
        ctypes.POINTER(_Overlapped),
    ]
    handle = msvcrt.get_osfhandle(fd)
    overlapped = _Overlapped()
    unlock_file_ex(handle, 0, 0xFFFFFFFF, 0xFFFFFFFF, ctypes.byref(overlapped))


# Backwards-compatible helper used by the test suite and external callers.
def ensure_lockfile(lock_path: str) -> None:
    # O_CREAT without O_EXCL: harmless if another process created it first.
    fd = os.open(lock_path, os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT, 0o600)
    os.close(fd)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Manifest (self-authenticating, atomically replaced)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


class AuditMetadataError(ValueError):
    """A tampered manifest or verify cache.

    Distinct from a malformed record line: damaged *metadata* is reported as
    chain corruption (verify returns ``ok=False``), whereas a half-written
    record keeps its existing bad-line semantics (ValueError, exit code 2).
    """


def default_manifest(first: str) -> dict:
    return {
        "version": 1,
        "active": first,
        "segments": [{"name": first, "sealed": False, "parts": []}],
    }


def _manifest_payload_text(manifest: dict) -> str:
    body = {
        "version": manifest["version"],
        "active": manifest["active"],
        "segments": manifest["segments"],
    }
    # The archive location is part of the signed body only when present, so
    # manifests written before two-tier storage existed keep their tags.
    if manifest.get("archive") is not None:
        body["archive"] = manifest["archive"]
    return rec.canonical_json(body)


def sign_manifest(manifest: dict) -> dict:
    """Return a manifest copy carrying its authentication tag."""
    signed = {
        "version": manifest["version"],
        "active": manifest["active"],
        "segments": manifest["segments"],
    }
    if manifest.get("archive") is not None:
        signed["archive"] = manifest["archive"]
    signed["tag"] = hashlib.sha256(
        _manifest_payload_text(signed).encode(_ENCODING)
    ).hexdigest()
    return signed


def load_manifest(layout: Layout) -> Optional[dict]:
    try:
        with open(layout.manifest_path, "rb") as handle:
            raw = handle.read()
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return None
    try:
        manifest = json.loads(raw.decode(_ENCODING))
    except (UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError) as exc:
        raise AuditMetadataError("malformed audit manifest") from exc
    if not isinstance(manifest, dict) or not _valid_manifest(manifest):
        raise AuditMetadataError("malformed audit manifest")
    tag = manifest.get("tag")
    if tag is not None:
        if not isinstance(tag, str):
            raise AuditMetadataError("tampered audit manifest")
        expected = hashlib.sha256(
            _manifest_payload_text(manifest).encode(_ENCODING)
        ).hexdigest()
        if not constant_time_equal(tag, expected):
            raise AuditMetadataError("tampered audit manifest")
    # A manifest without a tag was written by the pre-tag build: structurally
    # valid and accepted read-only; the next write re-signs it.
    return manifest


def _valid_manifest(manifest: Any) -> bool:
    if not isinstance(manifest, dict):
        return False
    if manifest.get("version") != 1 or not isinstance(manifest.get("active"), str):
        return False
    archive = manifest.get("archive")
    if archive is not None and not isinstance(archive, str):
        return False
    segments = manifest.get("segments")
    if not isinstance(segments, list) or not segments:
        return False
    for index, segment in enumerate(segments):
        if not isinstance(segment, dict):
            return False
        if not isinstance(segment.get("name"), str) or not isinstance(
            segment.get("sealed"), bool
        ):
            return False
        archived = segment.get("archived", False)
        if not isinstance(archived, bool):
            return False
        if archived:
            # An archived segment lives in the recorded archive location; it
            # is always sealed and never the active segment.
            if not archive or not segment["sealed"]:
                return False
            if segment["name"] == manifest["active"]:
                return False
        parts = segment.get("parts")
        if not isinstance(parts, list):
            return False
        for part in parts:
            if not _valid_part(part):
                return False
        if index == len(segments) - 1:
            if segment["name"] != manifest["active"] or segment["sealed"]:
                return False
        elif not segment["sealed"] or not parts:
            return False
    tag = manifest.get("tag")
    if tag is not None and not isinstance(tag, str):
        return False
    return True


def _valid_part(part: Any) -> bool:
    return (
        isinstance(part, dict)
        and isinstance(part.get("name"), str)
        and isinstance(part.get("size"), int)
        and isinstance(part.get("sha256"), str)
    )


def save_manifest(layout: Layout, manifest: dict) -> None:
    save_manifest_at(layout.data_dir, manifest)


def save_manifest_at(directory: str, manifest: dict) -> None:
    """Write a signed manifest into an arbitrary directory (e.g. staging)."""
    signed = sign_manifest(manifest)
    atomic_write_text(directory, MANIFEST_NAME, rec.canonical_json(signed))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Incremental verify cache
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def cache_tag_payload(version: int, segments: dict) -> bytes:
    return rec.canonical_json({"version": version, "segments": segments}).encode(
        _ENCODING
    )


def load_cache(layout: Layout) -> Optional[dict]:
    """Load the verify cache or return None when absent.

    A present cache whose authentication tag fails to verify is tampering:
    ``AuditMetadataError`` is raised rather than silently rebuilding, because
    reporting a clean pass off a forged cache must be impossible.
    """
    try:
        with open(layout.cache_path, "rb") as handle:
            raw = handle.read()
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return None
    try:
        cache = json.loads(raw.decode(_ENCODING))
    except (UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError) as exc:
        raise AuditMetadataError("tampered audit cache") from exc
    if not isinstance(cache, dict) or cache.get("version") != 1:
        raise AuditMetadataError("tampered audit cache")
    tag = cache.get("tag")
    segments = cache.get("segments")
    if not isinstance(tag, str) or not isinstance(segments, dict):
        raise AuditMetadataError("tampered audit cache")
    expected = hashlib.sha256(cache_tag_payload(1, segments)).hexdigest()
    if not constant_time_equal(tag, expected):
        raise AuditMetadataError("tampered audit cache")
    if not _valid_cache_segments(segments):
        raise AuditMetadataError("tampered audit cache")
    return {"version": 1, "segments": segments, "tag": tag}


def constant_time_equal(actual: str, expected: str) -> bool:
    if len(actual) != len(expected):
        return False
    result = 0
    for a, b in zip(actual, expected):
        result |= ord(a) ^ ord(b)
    return result == 0


def _valid_cache_segments(segments: Any) -> bool:
    if not isinstance(segments, dict):
        return False
    for name, entry in segments.items():
        if not isinstance(name, str) or not isinstance(entry, dict):
            return False
        if (
            not isinstance(entry.get("records"), int)
            or entry["records"] < 0
            or not isinstance(entry.get("size"), int)
            or entry["size"] < 0
            or not isinstance(entry.get("mtime_ns"), int)
            or not isinstance(entry.get("ctime_ns"), int)
        ):
            return False
        parts = entry.get("parts")
        if not isinstance(parts, list):
            return False
        for part in parts:
            if not _valid_part(part):
                return False
        # The fold is absent only in a structurally-valid pre-fold cache,
        # which the walker rebuilds from bytes; a present but malformed fold
        # cannot be trusted and is treated like any forged field.
        fold = entry.get("fold")
        if fold is not None:
            if not isinstance(fold, str) or len(fold) != 64:
                return False
            try:
                int(fold, 16)
            except ValueError:
                return False
        tenants = entry.get("tenants")
        if not isinstance(tenants, dict):
            return False
        for tenant, state in tenants.items():
            if not isinstance(tenant, str) or not isinstance(state, list):
                return False
            if len(state) != 3:
                return False
            count, digest, bad = state
            if (
                not isinstance(count, int)
                or not isinstance(digest, str)
                or not isinstance(bad, int)
                or count < 0
                or bad < -1
            ):
                return False
    return True


def save_cache(layout: Layout, segments: dict) -> None:
    tag = hashlib.sha256(cache_tag_payload(1, segments)).hexdigest()
    payload = {"version": 1, "segments": segments, "tag": tag}
    atomic_write_text(
        layout.cache_dir, layout.cache_name, rec.canonical_json(payload)
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Record scanning
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def scan_segment_bytes(path: str) -> bytes:
    with open(path, "rb") as handle:
        return handle.read()


def decode_records(raw: bytes) -> list[dict]:
    """Decode log bytes into validated records; bad/truncated lines raise."""
    try:
        text = raw.decode(_ENCODING)
    except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
        raise ValueError("malformed audit record") from exc
    return [rec.parse_line(line) for line in rec.split_records(text)]

"""Offline range proofs for a tenant's contiguous index interval.

A proof is self-contained JSON data:

* ``tenant``/``start``/``end``/``count`` name the interval and the total
  number of records the tenant had when it was exported;
* ``prev`` is the digest the first interval record must link from (``""``
  when the interval begins at index zero);
* ``windows`` is an ordered list of byte-window anchors. Each anchor names
  its global window sequence number (strictly increasing across segments,
  so the cross-segment window chain is explicit), carries the window's
  byte size and sha256, and lists the interval records that live in that
  window with their byte offset inside it. Only windows that hold an
  interval record appear, and the only payloads present are those of the
  interval itself -- no out-of-interval record ever leaves the exporter.

An independent reader needs nothing but this proof and the public digest
function in :mod:`audit_chain.record`: every record's digest is recomputed,
the predecessor links are checked, the indices are checked to be exactly
``start .. end-1``, offsets are checked to fall inside the anchored
windows, and the window sequence is checked to be strictly increasing.
Damage outside the interval cannot affect this conclusion because no
out-of-interval byte participates in the check.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from typing import Any, Optional

from . import record as rec

_HEX64 = re.compile(r"^[0-9a-f]{64}$")
PROOF_VERSION = 1


def empty_proof(tenant: str) -> dict:
    """The empty-history conclusion for a tenant with no records."""
    return {
        "version": PROOF_VERSION,
        "tenant": tenant,
        "start": 0,
        "end": 0,
        "count": 0,
        "prev": "",
        "windows": [],
    }


def build_proof(material: dict) -> dict:
    """Assemble the public proof object from exporter-collected material."""
    if material.get("count") == 0:
        return empty_proof(material["tenant"])

    windows = []
    for bucket in material["buckets"]:
        anchor = material["anchors"][bucket["seq"]]
        windows.append(
            {
                "seq": bucket["seq"],
                "name": anchor["name"],
                "size": anchor["size"],
                "sha256": anchor["sha256"],
                "records": [
                    {"index": index, "offset": offset, "record": dict(record)}
                    for index, offset, record in bucket["records"]
                ],
            }
        )
    return {
        "version": PROOF_VERSION,
        "tenant": material["tenant"],
        "start": material["start"],
        "end": material["end"],
        "count": material["count"],
        "prev": material["prev"],
        "windows": windows,
    }


def verify_proof(
    proof: Any,
    *,
    tenant: Optional[str] = None,
    start: Optional[int] = None,
    end: Optional[int] = None,
) -> dict:
    """Independently verify a range proof.

    Returns ``{"ok": bool, "first_bad": i, "count": n, "start": s,
    "end": e, "tenant": t}`` where ``first_bad`` is the global tenant index
    of the first record that fails to link, is mis-indexed, or does not sit
    inside its anchored window. A structurally malformed proof raises
    ``ValueError``. Optional ``tenant``/``start``/``end`` bind the caller's
    request to the proof.
    """
    _require(
        isinstance(proof, dict) and proof.get("version") == PROOF_VERSION,
        "malformed range proof",
    )
    p_tenant = proof.get("tenant")
    p_start = proof.get("start")
    p_end = proof.get("end")
    p_count = proof.get("count")
    p_prev = proof.get("prev")
    windows = proof.get("windows")
    _require(isinstance(p_tenant, str), "malformed range proof: tenant")
    _require(_nonneg_int(p_start), "malformed range proof: start")
    _require(_nonneg_int(p_end), "malformed range proof: end")
    _require(_nonneg_int(p_count), "malformed range proof: count")
    _require(isinstance(p_prev, str), "malformed range proof: prev")
    _require(isinstance(windows, list), "malformed range proof: windows")
    if tenant is not None:
        _require(tenant == p_tenant, "proof is for a different tenant")
    if start is not None:
        _require(start == p_start, "proof covers a different start")
    if end is not None:
        _require(end == p_end, "proof covers a different end")

    if p_count == 0:
        _require(
            p_start == 0 and p_end == 0 and p_prev == "" and windows == [],
            "malformed empty proof",
        )
        return _verdict(p_tenant, 0, 0, -1)

    _require(p_start < p_end, "malformed range proof: empty interval")
    _require(p_end <= p_count, "malformed range proof: interval past history")

    first_bad = -1
    seen = 0
    previous_seq: Optional[int] = None
    expected_index = p_start
    expected_digest = p_prev

    def flag(index: int) -> None:
        nonlocal first_bad
        if first_bad == -1:
            first_bad = index

    for window in windows:
        _require(isinstance(window, dict), "malformed range proof: window")
        seq = window.get("seq")
        size = window.get("size")
        sha = window.get("sha256")
        records = window.get("records")
        _require(_nonneg_int(seq), "malformed range proof: window seq")
        _require(_nonneg_int(size), "malformed range proof: window size")
        _require(isinstance(sha, str) and bool(_HEX64.match(sha)), "bad window anchor")
        _require(
            isinstance(records, list) and records,
            "malformed range proof: window without records",
        )
        if previous_seq is not None and seq <= previous_seq:
            # Cross-segment windows must form a strictly increasing chain.
            flag(p_start)
        previous_seq = seq

        previous_offset = -1
        for item in records:
            _require(isinstance(item, dict), "malformed range proof: record slot")
            index = item.get("index")
            offset = item.get("offset")
            record = item.get("record")
            _require(_nonneg_int(index), "malformed range proof: record index")
            _require(_nonneg_int(offset), "malformed range proof: record offset")
            if index != expected_index:
                flag(expected_index)
            if offset <= previous_offset:
                flag(index)
            previous_offset = offset

            try:
                parsed = (
                    rec.parse_line(rec.canonical_json(record))
                    if isinstance(record, dict)
                    else None
                )
            except ValueError:
                parsed = None
            if parsed is None:
                flag(index)
                expected_index = index + 1
                seen += 1
                continue

            line_len = len((rec.canonical_json(parsed) + "\n").encode("utf-8"))
            if offset + line_len > size:
                # The record does not live inside the anchored window.
                flag(index)
            if parsed["tenant"] != p_tenant:
                flag(index)
            recomputed = rec.digest(parsed["prev"], parsed["payload"])
            if parsed["prev"] != expected_digest or parsed["digest"] != recomputed:
                flag(index)
            else:
                expected_digest = parsed["digest"]
            expected_index = index + 1
            seen += 1

    if seen != p_end - p_start:
        flag(p_start)
    if expected_index != p_end:
        flag(p_end)
    return _verdict(p_tenant, p_start, p_end, first_bad)


def combine_proofs(left: Any, right: Any) -> dict:
    """Splice two contiguous proofs of the same tenant into one proof.

    The interval of ``right`` must begin exactly where ``left`` ends
    (``left["end"] == right["start"]``); the result then covers the union
    ``[left["start"], right["end"])`` and is itself an ordinary version-1
    proof verifiable through :func:`verify_proof`. The combined proof is
    re-verified before it is returned, so splicing can never produce a proof
    that does not independently check out.

    A non-dict argument raises ``TypeError`` (the same rule the on-chain
    append uses for its payload). Anything else that is not a legally
    exported, independently verifiable proof -- a tenant mismatch, a gap, an
    overlap, a reversed order, or a side that fails verification -- raises
    ``ValueError`` and yields no result.
    """
    if not isinstance(left, dict) or not isinstance(right, dict):
        raise TypeError("proofs must be dicts")

    # Both sides must be genuine exported proofs and must independently check
    # out before any splicing is attempted.
    try:
        left_verdict = verify_proof(left)
        right_verdict = verify_proof(right)
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise ValueError("cannot combine: proof is not a valid range proof") from exc
    if not left_verdict["ok"] or not right_verdict["ok"]:
        raise ValueError("cannot combine: a proof does not independently verify")

    if left["tenant"] != right["tenant"]:
        raise ValueError("cannot combine: proofs are for different tenants")
    if left["end"] != right["start"]:
        # One message covers gap, overlap and reversed ordering: the only
        # accepted relation is end-of-left exactly touching start-of-right.
        raise ValueError("cannot combine: intervals are not contiguous")

    if left["count"] == 0:
        # The empty-history proof only touches a non-empty proof at zero;
        # the union is then exactly the right side.
        merged_windows = [_clone_window(window) for window in right["windows"]]
    elif right["count"] == 0:
        merged_windows = [_clone_window(window) for window in left["windows"]]
    else:
        merged_windows = [_clone_window(window) for window in left["windows"]]
        first_right = right["windows"][0] if right["windows"] else None
        boundary = merged_windows[-1] if merged_windows else None
        if (
            boundary is not None
            and first_right is not None
            and _same_anchor(boundary, first_right)
        ):
            # The split landed inside one physical byte window: keep one
            # window and concatenate the records in index order.
            boundary["records"].extend(_clone_slot(slot) for slot in first_right["records"])
            rest = right["windows"][1:]
        else:
            rest = right["windows"]
        merged_windows.extend(_clone_window(window) for window in rest)

    # Seq numbers are local to each export, so renumber the merged chain from
    # zero; verification only relies on them being strictly increasing.
    for seq, window in enumerate(merged_windows):
        window["seq"] = seq

    combined = {
        "version": PROOF_VERSION,
        "tenant": left["tenant"],
        "start": left["start"],
        "end": right["end"],
        "count": max(left["count"], right["count"]),
        "prev": left["prev"],
        "windows": merged_windows,
    }
    verdict = verify_proof(combined)
    if not verdict["ok"]:
        raise ValueError("cannot combine: combined proof does not verify")
    return combined


def verify_proofs(proofs: Any) -> list[dict]:
    """Verify a batch of proofs, one verdict per proof, in input order.

    Each verdict has exactly the shape the on-chain ``Chain.verify`` returns
    -- ``{"ok": bool, "first_bad": i, "count": n}`` and nothing else. A proof
    whose content was tampered with yields an ``ok=False`` verdict carrying
    the real first bad index; verification of the remaining proofs continues.
    A structurally malformed proof likewise yields a corrupted verdict
    instead of interrupting the batch.

    The list itself being empty raises ``ValueError``; the argument or any
    element not being a dict raises ``TypeError``.
    """
    if not isinstance(proofs, list):
        raise TypeError("proofs must be a list")
    if not proofs:
        raise ValueError("proofs list must not be empty")

    verdicts: list[dict] = []
    for proof in proofs:
        if not isinstance(proof, dict):
            raise TypeError("each proof must be a dict")
        try:
            verdicts.append(_chain_verdict(verify_proof(proof)))
        except ValueError:
            # Structurally malformed: no chain walk was possible, so there is
            # no record-derived bad index. Report corruption at the earliest
            # index the proof itself claims, keeping the verdict shape.
            verdicts.append(_corrupted_verdict(proof))
    return verdicts


def _same_anchor(a: dict, b: dict) -> bool:
    return (
        a["name"] == b["name"] and a["size"] == b["size"] and a["sha256"] == b["sha256"]
    )


def _clone_slot(slot: dict) -> dict:
    return {
        "index": slot["index"],
        "offset": slot["offset"],
        "record": dict(slot["record"]),
    }


def _clone_window(window: dict) -> dict:
    return {
        "seq": window["seq"],
        "name": window["name"],
        "size": window["size"],
        "sha256": window["sha256"],
        "records": [_clone_slot(slot) for slot in window["records"]],
    }


def _chain_verdict(verdict: dict) -> dict:
    """Project a proof verdict onto the on-chain verdict's three keys."""
    return {
        "ok": verdict["ok"],
        "first_bad": verdict["first_bad"],
        "count": verdict["count"],
    }


def _corrupted_verdict(proof: dict) -> dict:
    start = proof.get("start")
    end = proof.get("end")
    if not _nonneg_int(start):
        start = 0
    if not _nonneg_int(end) or end < start:
        end = start
    return {
        "ok": False,
        "first_bad": start,
        "count": end - start,
    }


def _verdict(tenant: str, start: int, end: int, first_bad: int) -> dict:
    return {
        "ok": first_bad == -1,
        "first_bad": first_bad,
        "count": end - start,
        "start": start,
        "end": end,
        "tenant": tenant,
    }


def _require(condition: bool, message: str) -> None:
    if not condition:
        raise ValueError(message)


def _nonneg_int(value: Any) -> bool:
    return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool) and value >= 0

4	be walked offline and the first tampered index pinpointed. Tenants are
5	independent chains that share one physical log.

8	semantics:
9	
10	* concurrent appenders to the same log are serialized by a process-shared,
11	  cross-platform file lock, so interlocked writes still link strictly;
12	* every read (``verify``/``entries``/``head``) takes a snapshot under a
13	  shared lock: a single call always sees one complete prefix -- the old
14	  topology or the new one around a rotation, merge or recovery -- never a
15	  mix of segments, a duplicate run or a skipped run;
16	* the log can be rotated into ordered segment files and compacted, with
17	  every source segment's verification material (byte size + sha256)
18	  retained through merges, committed by an atomic, self-authenticating
19	  manifest replacement; merged bytes are published through a temp file and
20	  rename, so every crash window lands on the old or the new topology;
21	* sealed segments can be migrated online into a caller-specified archive
22	  directory (cold tier): the signed manifest records the archive location
23	  and keeps every migrated segment's window material, so append, query,
24	  verify, rotate, compact, recover and export all work unchanged across
25	  the two tiers, and a process killed mid-migration reopens onto either
26	  the pre-archive or the complete post-archive topology -- never a half
27	  moved segment or copies left in both tiers;
28	* verification of long logs is incremental: unchanged byte windows are
29	  authenticated by an on-disk cache (stat-guarded on the active unit,
30	  window-material-guarded on sealed units), so a repeated verification of
31	  a ten-thousand-entry log only hashes newly appended bytes plus a small
32	  amount of sidecar material;
33	* tampering with the cache, the manifest or a sealed window is reported as
34	  chain corruption with the real first bad global index (never a pass, and
35	  distinct from the half-line bad-line semantics);
36	* ``export_range`` produces an offline proof for a contiguous index

367	                # nor silently healed: re-derive from bytes and report the
368	                # metadata damage as corruption below.
369	                metadata_damaged = True
370	                states, _ = self._walk(units, layout, ignore_cache=True, persist=False)
371	
372	        state = states.get(tenant)
373	        if state is None:
374	            return {"count": 0, "first_bad": -1, "ok": True}
375	        count, _head, bad = state
376	        if bad != -1:
377	            # The byte-level walk found the real break first; it always
378	            # outranks the metadata tripwire.
379	            return {"count": count, "first_bad": bad, "ok": False}
380	        if metadata_damaged:
381	            # The bytes still re-derive, but authentication material the
382	            # chain depended on (manifest windows or the verified cache) was
383	            # rewritten: the earliest index it could vouch for is 0.
384	            return {"count": count, "first_bad": 0, "ok": False}
385	        return {"count": count, "first_bad": -1, "ok": True}
386	
387	    def _require_present(self, layout: st.Layout) -> None:
388	        if layout.kind == "file":
389	            if not os.path.isfile(layout.root):
390	                raise FileNotFoundError(layout.root)
391	            return
392	        # An existing directory without a manifest is malformed; let the
393	        # view report it rather than masking it as a missing file.
394	        if not os.path.isdir(layout.root):
395	            raise FileNotFoundError(layout.root)
396	
397	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
398	    # Append
399	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
400	
401	    def append(self, tenant: str, payload: Any) -> dict:
402	        """Append one record for ``tenant`` and return the stored entry.
403	
404	        Raises ``TypeError`` for a non-object payload and ``ValueError`` if
405	        the existing log, its cache or its manifest is corrupt; existing
406	        records are left untouched. Concurrent appenders are serialized by
407	        a file lock.
408	        """
409	        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
410	            raise TypeError("payload must be a dict")
411	
412	        with self._locked(exclusive=True) as layout:
413	            units = self._view(layout)
414	
415	            # Refuse to extend a damaged log.
416	            states, entries = self._walk(units, layout)
417	            for _count, _head, bad in states.values():
418	                if bad != -1:
419	                    raise ValueError("corrupt audit chain")
420	
421	            prev = states.get(tenant, (0, "", -1))[1]
422	            record, line = rec.build_line(tenant, payload, prev)
423	            target = units[-1]["path"]
424	            data = (line + "\n").encode(_ENCODING)
425	            # Two raw writes with a real kill point between them model the
426	            # write/flush/fsync crash window: a kill after the first syscall
427	            # leaves a deterministic half line that reopen treats as a bad
428	            # line, never as a silently repaired record.
429	            cut = max(1, len(data) // 2)
430	            fd = os.open(target, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_APPEND, 0o600)
431	            try:
432	                _write_all(fd, data[:cut])
433	                st.crash_point("append:after_first_write")
434	                _write_all(fd, data[cut:])
435	                st.crash_point("append:before_fsync")
436	                os.fsync(fd)
437	                st.crash_point("append:after_fsync")
438	            finally:
439	                os.close(fd)
440	
441	            # Warm the cache with the single record just written: suffix
442	            # only, never a rehash of the whole file. The continuation is
443	            # computed from the entries this same locked section
444	            # authenticated above -- the cache file is not re-read here, so
445	            # nothing swapped onto disk behind the walk can be laundered
446	            # into a trusted prefix.
447	            self._warm_append_cache(layout, units[-1], entries, states, record, line)
448	        return record
449	
450	    def _warm_append_cache(
451	        self,
452	        layout: st.Layout,
453	        unit: dict,
454	        entries: dict,
455	        states: dict,
456	        record: dict,
457	        line: str,
458	    ) -> None:
459	        """Extend the just-authenticated cache with one appended record.
460	
461	        ``entries``/``states`` come from the verification walk that ran
462	        under the same exclusive lock moments before the record was
463	        written, so the cached prefix they describe was authenticated in
464	        this critical section; only the new line is hashed on top of it.
465	        """
466	        name = unit["name"]
467	        line_bytes = (line + "\n").encode(_ENCODING)
468	        continued = {tenant: list(state) for tenant, state in states.items()}
469	        count, _head, bad = continued.get(record["tenant"], [0, "", -1])
470	        continued[record["tenant"]] = [count + 1, record["digest"], bad]
471	        entry = entries.get(name)
472	        if entry is None:
473	            # First append to a unit that did not exist at walk time.
474	            records, parts, fold = 0, [dict(p) for p in unit["parts"]], _FOLD_BLANK
475	        else:
476	            records = entry["records"]
477	            parts = entry.get("parts", [])
478	            fold = entry["fold"]
479	        entries[name] = _cache_entry(
480	            records + 1,
481	            os.stat(unit["path"]),
482	            parts,
483	            continued,
484	            _extend_fold(fold, [line_bytes]),
485	        )
486	        st.save_cache(layout, entries)
487	
488	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
489	    # Crash recovery
490	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
491	
492	    def recover(self) -> dict:
493	        """Truncate a half-written tail line left by a crashed append.
494	
495	        Only the physical trailing partial line of the active log is
496	        removed; complete but chain-broken records are never silently
497	        repaired. Returns the number of bytes removed. The verify cache is
498	        discarded because the bytes legitimately shrank.
499	        """
500	        with self._locked(exclusive=True) as layout:
501	            self._require_present(layout)
502	            units = self._view(layout)
503	            target = units[-1]["path"]
504	
505	            with open(target, "rb") as handle:
506	                raw = handle.read()
507	            if raw == b"" or raw.endswith(b"\n"):
508	                return {"truncated_bytes": 0}
509	
510	            cut = raw.rfind(b"\n") + 1
511	            removed = len(raw) - cut
512	            # Drop the cache before changing bytes: whichever window a kill
513	            # lands in, reopen never mistakes the legitimate shrink for a
514	            # cached deletion (either the half line still reads as a bad
515	            # line, or the cache is already gone and the prefix re-derives).
516	            self._delete_cache(layout)
517	            fd = os.open(target, os.O_WRONLY)
518	            try:
519	                os.ftruncate(fd, cut)
520	                st.crash_point("recover:after_truncate")
521	                os.fsync(fd)
522	            finally:
523	                os.close(fd)
524	        return {"truncated_bytes": removed}
525	
526	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
527	    # Rotation and compaction
528	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
529	
530	    def rotate(self) -> None:
531	        """Cut a new active segment.
532	
533	        On a legacy single-file log this first migrates the file into a
534	        segment store at the same path, sealing the original bytes as the
535	        first segment. On an already segmented log the active segment is
536	        sealed (its preserved windows plus one window for the bytes appended
537	        after them) and a fresh empty segment becomes active.
538	        """
539	        with self._locked(exclusive=True) as layout:
540	            if layout.kind == "file":
541	                self._migrate_file(layout)
542	            else:
543	                self._rotate_dir(layout)
544	
545	    def _migrate_file(self, layout: st.Layout) -> None:
546	        path = layout.root
547	        raw = b""
548	        if os.path.exists(path):
549	            with open(path, "rb") as handle:
550	                raw = handle.read()
551	            # A crashed half-line must be recovered, not silently migrated.
552	            st.decode_records(raw)
553	
554	        parent = os.path.dirname(path) or "."
555	        staging = path + ".segstage"
556	        backup = path + ".pre-segment"
557	        if os.path.exists(backup):
558	            os.remove(backup)
559	        os.mkdir(staging)
560	        try:
561	            if raw:
562	                first = st.seg_name(st.FIRST_SEQ)
563	                second = st.seg_name(st.FIRST_SEQ + 1)
564	                self._write_bytes(staging, first, raw)
565	                self._write_bytes(staging, second, b"")
566	                manifest = {
567	                    "version": 1,
568	                    "active": second,
569	                    "segments": [
570	                        {
571	                            "name": first,
572	                            "sealed": True,
573	                            "parts": [
574	                                {
575	                                    "name": first,
576	                                    "size": len(raw),
577	                                    "sha256": _sha256(raw),
578	                                }
579	                            ],
580	                        },
581	                        {"name": second, "sealed": False, "parts": []},
582	                    ],
583	                }
584	            else:
585	                first = st.seg_name(st.FIRST_SEQ)
586	                self._write_bytes(staging, first, b"")
587	                manifest = st.default_manifest(first)
588	            st.save_manifest_at(staging, manifest)
589	            st.crash_point("migrate:after_staging")
590	
591	            # Keep the old data until the new store is in place: rename it
592	            # aside, publish the store, then drop the backup. Every kill in
593	            # between lands on one topology and is healed on next open.
594	            committed = False
595	            if os.path.exists(path):
596	                os.replace(path, backup)
597	                st.fsync_dir(parent)
598	            st.crash_point("migrate:after_backup_rename")
599	            try:
600	                os.replace(staging, path)
601	                st.fsync_dir(parent)
602	                committed = True
603	            finally:
604	                if not committed:
605	                    with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
606	                        os.replace(backup, path)
607	                        st.fsync_dir(parent)
608	            st.crash_point("migrate:after_publish")
609	            if os.path.exists(backup):
610	                os.remove(backup)
611	                st.fsync_dir(parent)
612	        except BaseException:
613	            # Roll the staging directory back out; the original file lives on
614	            # as the backup until the new store is fully published.
615	            if os.path.isdir(staging):
616	                for name in os.listdir(staging):
617	                    with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
618	                        os.unlink(os.path.join(staging, name))
619	                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
620	                    os.rmdir(staging)
621	            raise
622	
623	        # The lock is topology-independent and stays put; the legacy sidecar
624	        # described the former single file, whereas the store's cache lives
625	        # inside the directory. Drop the stale one and warm the store's cache
626	        # from the bytes just migrated (mirrors _rotate_dir), so an export
627	        # right after the first rotation need not cold-scan the history.
628	        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
629	            os.remove(layout.cache_path)
630	        new_layout = st.Layout(self.path, "dir")
631	        with contextlib.suppress(OSError, ValueError):
632	            self._walk(self._view(new_layout), new_layout)
633	
634	    def _rotate_dir(self, layout: st.Layout) -> None:
635	        units = self._view(layout)
636	        manifest = st.load_manifest(layout)
637	        active_name = manifest["active"]
638	        active_unit = next(unit for unit in units if unit["name"] == active_name)
639	        active_manifest = next(
640	            segment for segment in manifest["segments"] if segment["name"] == active_name
641	        )
642	        size = os.path.getsize(active_unit["path"])
643	        if size == 0:
644	            return
645	
646	        # Walk first so a corrupt active segment cannot be sealed away.
647	        states, entries = self._walk(units, layout)
648	        for _count, _head, bad in states.values():
649	            if bad != -1:
650	                raise ValueError("corrupt audit chain")
651	
652	        # Freeze the active bytes as verification material: keep windows the
653	        # segment already preserved (e.g. from a fold-to-one compaction) and
654	        # add one window for the bytes appended after them.
655	        with open(active_unit["path"], "rb") as handle:
656	            active_bytes = handle.read()
657	        sealed_prefix = sum(part["size"] for part in active_manifest["parts"])
658	        seal_parts = [dict(part) for part in active_manifest["parts"]]
659	        if seal_parts and not st.verify_prefix_windows(
660	            active_unit["path"], seal_parts
661	        ):
662	            raise ValueError("corrupt audit segment")
663	        if len(active_bytes) > sealed_prefix:
664	            seal_parts.append(
665	                {
666	                    "name": active_name,
667	                    "size": len(active_bytes) - sealed_prefix,
668	                    "sha256": _sha256(active_bytes[sealed_prefix:]),
669	                }
670	            )
671	        entries[active_name]["parts"] = [dict(part) for part in seal_parts]
672	        for segment in manifest["segments"]:
673	            if segment["name"] == active_name:
674	                segment["sealed"] = True
675	                segment["parts"] = seal_parts
676	        next_seq = max(st.seg_seq(s["name"]) for s in manifest["segments"]) + 1
677	        new_active = st.seg_name(next_seq)
678	        # The new segment is an unreferenced orphan until the manifest commit
679	        # names it; a kill in this window simply has it garbage-collected and
680	        # the old topology remains authoritative.
681	        self._write_bytes(layout.root, new_active, b"")
682	        st.crash_point("rotate:before_manifest")
683	        manifest["segments"].append(
684	            {"name": new_active, "sealed": False, "parts": []}
685	        )
686	        manifest["active"] = new_active
687	        st.save_manifest(layout, manifest)
688	        st.crash_point("rotate:after_manifest")
689	        st.save_cache(layout, entries)
690	
691	    def compact(self, max_segments: int = _DEFAULT_MAX_SEGMENTS) -> dict:
692	        """Merge old sealed segments while keeping each one's material.
693	
694	        The log is folded until at most ``max_segments`` segments remain
695	        (the active segment counts). Each merge concatenates the source
696	        bytes and retains their ordered (size, sha256) windows, so every
697	        source segment's verification material survives compression and the
698	        global insertion order is unchanged.
699	
700	        Merged bytes are staged in a temp file and renamed before the
701	        atomic manifest commit; the old segments are removed only after the
702	        commit. A kill at any point therefore leaves the old topology or
703	        the complete new topology plus unreferenced files reaped on reopen.
704	        """
705	        if max_segments < 1:
706	            raise ValueError("max_segments must be >= 1")
707	        with self._locked(exclusive=True) as layout:
708	            if layout.kind != "dir":
709	                raise ValueError("log is not segmented; call rotate() first")
710	            units = self._view(layout)
711	
712	            # Never fold a damaged log.
713	            states, _ = self._walk(units, layout)
714	            for _count, _head, bad in states.values():
715	                if bad != -1:
716	                    raise ValueError("corrupt audit chain")
717	
718	            manifest = st.load_manifest(layout)
719	            cache = st.load_cache(layout)
720	            cache_segments = {} if cache is None else dict(cache["segments"])
721	
722	            if max_segments == 1 and len(manifest["segments"]) > 1:
723	                removed = self._merge_all(layout, manifest, cache_segments)
724	            else:
725	                removed: list[dict] = []
726	                while len(manifest["segments"]) > max_segments:
727	                    removed += self._merge_pair(layout, manifest, cache_segments)
728	
729	            if removed:
730	                # Commit the new topology first; the now-unreferenced
731	                # sources are removed after the durable manifest swap and
732	                # otherwise garbage collected on the next open, so a crash
733	                # never loses data and never exposes a mixed topology.
734	                st.save_manifest(layout, manifest)
735	                st.crash_point("compact:after_manifest")
736	                st.save_cache(layout, cache_segments)
737	                for source in removed:
738	                    with contextlib.suppress(FileNotFoundError):
739	                        os.remove(self._segment_path(layout, manifest, source))
740	                    st.crash_point("compact:during_delete")
741	                st.fsync_dir(layout.root)
742	                st.crash_point("compact:after_delete")
743	            count = len(manifest["segments"])
744	        return {"segments": count}
745	
746	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
747	    # Online archiving (cold tier)
748	    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
749	
750	    def archive(self, archive_dir: str) -> dict:
751	        """Migrate every sealed segment to ``archive_dir``, online.
752	
753	        The archive location is caller-specified and recorded in the
754	        self-authenticating manifest, so every later open of this store
755	        resolves archived segments across the two tiers with no extra
756	        arguments. Migrated segments keep their names, window material and
757	        position in the manifest: per-tenant indices, rotation order,
758	        verdicts and exported proofs are exactly what they were before the
759	        move, and the hot directory no longer holds the migrated bytes.
760	
761	        The migration is online and crash-safe. It runs under the same
762	        exclusive lock as append/rotate/compact, so a concurrent caller
763	        always observes one complete prefix -- the pre-archive or the
764	        post-archive topology, never a mix. The location is committed
765	        first, then every segment is copied through a temp file + fsync +
766	        atomic rename, then a second manifest commit marks the segments
767	        archived, and only then are the hot copies removed. A process
768	        killed in any window reopens onto one complete topology: staged
769	        copies, orphans and hot duplicates are reaped deterministically,
770	        and no segment is ever lost or left in both tiers.
771	
772	        Returns ``{"archived": n}`` -- the number of segments this call
773	        migrated (zero when every sealed segment is already archived).
774	        Raises ``ValueError`` on a legacy file layout (rotate first), a
775	        corrupt chain, an archive directory inside the store itself, or a
776	        different location than an earlier archive call recorded.
777	        """
778	        dest = os.path.abspath(os.fspath(archive_dir))
779	        with self._locked(exclusive=True) as layout:
780	            if layout.kind != "dir":
781	                raise ValueError("log is not segmented; call rotate() first")
782	            if os.path.normpath(dest) == os.path.normpath(
783	                os.path.abspath(layout.root)
784	            ):
785	                raise ValueError("archive directory must differ from the store")
786	            if os.path.exists(os.path.join(dest, st.MANIFEST_NAME)):
787	                raise ValueError("archive directory is itself a segment store")
788	            units = self._view(layout)
789	            manifest = st.load_manifest(layout)
790	
791	            # Never migrate a damaged log.
792	            states, _ = self._walk(units, layout)
793	            for _count, _head, bad in states.values():
794	                if bad != -1:
795	                    raise ValueError("corrupt audit chain")
796	
797	            recorded = manifest.get("archive")
798	            if recorded is not None and os.path.normpath(recorded) != os.path.normpath(
799	                dest
800	            ):
801	                raise ValueError("log already archives to a different location")
802	
803	            targets = [
804	                segment
805	                for segment in manifest["segments"]
806	                if segment["sealed"] and not segment.get("archived")
807	            ]
808	            if not targets:
809	                return {"archived": 0}
810	
811	            os.makedirs(dest, exist_ok=True)
812	            # Raise the in-flight marker before the first commit: until the
813	            # migration is fully settled the marker tells every reopening
814	            # reader/writer to finish the tier housekeeping first, so a
815	            # kill anywhere in the middle never reopens onto copies kept in
816	            # both tiers.
817	            marker = os.path.join(layout.root, _ARCHIVE_MARKER)
818	            fd = os.open(marker, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_TRUNC, 0o600)
819	            os.close(fd)
820	            st.fsync_dir(layout.root)
821	            st.crash_point("archive:after_marker")
822	            if recorded is None:
823	                # Commit the location first: a kill during the copies then
824	                # still reopens knowing where staged bytes may lie, and the
825	                # reaper settles the tree back onto the hot-only topology.
826	                manifest["archive"] = dest
827	                st.save_manifest(layout, manifest)
828	                st.crash_point("archive:after_location")
829	
830	            for segment in targets:
831	                source = layout.segment_path(segment["name"])
832	                # The pre-walk may have vouched for this segment from the
833	                # authenticated cache alone; re-check its frozen windows
834	                # against the bytes before they become the only copy.
835	                if not st.verify_windows(source, segment["parts"]):
836	                    raise ValueError("corrupt audit segment")
837	                with open(source, "rb") as handle:
838	                    raw = handle.read()
839	                self._publish_bytes(dest, segment["name"], raw, phase="archive", kind="copy")
840	                st.crash_point("archive:after_copy")
841	
842	            migrated = {segment["name"] for segment in targets}
843	            for segment in manifest["segments"]:
844	                if segment["name"] in migrated:
845	                    segment["archived"] = True
846	            st.save_manifest(layout, manifest)
847	            st.crash_point("archive:after_manifest")
848	
849	            # Keep the verify cache warm across the move: the bytes are
850	            # identical, only each migrated segment's stat identity changed.
851	            cache = st.load_cache(layout)
852	            if cache is not None:
853	                cached_segments = cache["segments"]
854	                changed = False
855	                for name in migrated:
856	                    entry = cached_segments.get(name)
857	                    if entry is not None:
858	                        new_stat = os.stat(os.path.join(dest, name))
859	                        entry["size"] = new_stat.st_size
860	                        entry["mtime_ns"] = new_stat.st_mtime_ns
861	                        entry["ctime_ns"] = new_stat.st_ctime_ns
862	                        changed = True
863	                if changed:
864	                    st.save_cache(layout, cached_segments)
865	
866	            # The post-archive topology is durable; the hot copies are now
867	            # unreferenced and their removal is completed (or reaped on the
868	            # next open) without ever exposing a mixed topology.
869	            for name in migrated:
870	                with contextlib.suppress(FileNotFoundError):
871	                    os.remove(layout.segment_path(name))
872	                st.crash_point("archive:during_delete")
873	            st.fsync_dir(layout.root)
874	            # Settled: lower the in-flight marker last of all.
875	            with contextlib.suppress(FileNotFoundError):
876	                os.remove(marker)
877	            st.fsync_dir(layout.root)
878	            st.crash_point("archive:after_delete")
879	        return {"archived": len(migrated)}
880	
881	    def _gc_segments(self, layout: st.Layout, manifest: dict) -> None:
882	        """Remove segment files not referenced by the committed manifest."""
883	        referenced = {segment["name"] for segment in manifest["segments"]}
884	        changed = False
885	        for name in os.listdir(layout.root):
886	            if st.seg_seq(name) is not None and name not in referenced:
887	                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
888	                    os.remove(layout.segment_path(name))
889	                    changed = True
890	        if changed:
891	            st.fsync_dir(layout.root)
