893	    def _gc_archive(self, layout: st.Layout, manifest: dict) -> None:
894	        """Settle an archived store onto exactly one topology.
895	
896	        A migration killed after its manifest commit leaves hot duplicates
897	        of archived segments; one killed before it leaves copied-but-
898	        unreferenced segments (or staging temp files) in the archive
899	        directory. Both are removed here so a reopened store never keeps
900	        copies of one segment in the two tiers.
901	        """
902	        archive_dir = manifest.get("archive")
903	        if not archive_dir:
904	            return
905	        changed = False
906	        for segment in manifest["segments"]:
907	            if not segment.get("archived"):
908	                continue
909	            hot = layout.segment_path(segment["name"])
910	            if os.path.exists(hot):
911	                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
912	                    os.remove(hot)
913	                    changed = True
914	        if changed:
915	            st.fsync_dir(layout.root)
916	        if not os.path.isdir(archive_dir):
917	            return
918	        archived = {
919	            segment["name"] for segment in manifest["segments"] if segment.get("archived")
920	        }
921	        changed = False
922	        for name in os.listdir(archive_dir):
923	            # The archive tier holds exactly the segments the committed
924	            # manifest marks archived; any other segment file here is a
925	            # staged copy or merge orphan whose authoritative bytes live
926	            # in the hot tier.
927	            if (st.seg_seq(name) is not None and name not in archived) or (
928	                name.startswith(".") and name.endswith(".tmp")
929	            ):
930	                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
931	                    os.remove(os.path.join(archive_dir, name))

1021	    def _compose(
1022	        self,
1023	        layout: st.Layout,
1024	        manifest: dict,
1025	        sources: list[dict],
1026	        cache_segments: dict,
1027	    ) -> tuple[bytes, list[dict], Optional[dict]]:
1028	        """Concatenate source bytes and windows, carrying warm cached states."""
1029	        chunks: list[bytes] = []
1030	        parts: list[dict] = []
1031	        for source in sources:
1032	            path = self._segment_path(layout, manifest, source)
1033	            with open(path, "rb") as handle:
1034	                data = handle.read()
1035	            if source["sealed"]:
1036	                windows = source["parts"]
1037	                if len(data) != sum(w["size"] for w in windows) or not st.verify_windows(
1038	                    path, windows
1039	                ):
1040	                    raise ValueError("corrupt audit segment")
1041	            else:
1042	                # The active segment carries no preserved byte windows;
1043	                # freeze one full-content window for it now (read once).
1044	                windows = [
1045	                    {
1046	                        "name": source["name"],
1047	                        "size": len(data),
1048	                        "sha256": _sha256(data),
1049	                    }
1050	                ]
1051	            chunks.append(data)
1052	            parts.extend(dict(part) for part in windows)
1053	
1054	        # Cache entries hold cumulative per-tenant states, so after the
1055	        # sources in order the last cached entry describes the whole merge.
1056	        carried: Optional[dict] = None
1057	        for source in sources:
1058	            cached = cache_segments.get(source["name"])
1059	            if cached is None:
1060	                carried = None
1061	                break
1062	            carried = {
1063	                "records": cached["records"],
1064	                "tenants": {
1065	                    tenant: list(state) for tenant, state in cached["tenants"].items()
1066	                },
1067	            }
1068	        return b"".join(chunks), parts, carried

1075	    def _walk(
1076	        self,
1077	        units: list[dict],
1078	        layout: st.Layout,
1079	        *,
1080	        ignore_cache: bool = False,
1081	        persist: bool = True,
1082	    ) -> tuple[dict[str, tuple[int, int, int]], dict]:
1083	        """Walk every unit in order, reusing authenticated cached prefixes.
1084	
1085	        Returns ``(states, entries)``: states maps tenant to
1086	        ``(count, head_digest, first_bad)``; entries maps unit name to its
1087	        cache entry. Cost model:
1088	
1089	        * a unit unchanged since caching adopts the cached states with no
1090	          record reads or digest work -- the active unit is stat-guarded and
1091	          a sealed unit is guarded by its preserved window material, so no
1092	          sealed byte is hashed on the hot path;
1093	        * a grown active/legacy unit parses and chains only the appended
1094	          suffix, so a ten-thousand-entry re-verify never rehashes the file;
1095	        * a sealed segment is authenticated by its preserved byte windows
1096	          (merged segments keep one window per source segment), and damaged
1097	          windows are attributed to the tenants whose records they hold, so
1098	          one tenant's corruption never changes another tenant's verdict
1099	          while ``first_bad`` stays the global per-tenant index.
1100	        """
1101	        cache = None if ignore_cache else st.load_cache(layout)
1102	        cached = {} if cache is None else cache["segments"]
1103	        states: dict[str, list] = {}
1104	        entries: dict[str, dict] = {}
1105	        total_records = 0
1106	        # Once any unit is re-walked outside its cache, the cached cumulative
1107	        # states of every later unit were derived from the old prefix and can
1108	        # no longer be adopted: cross-boundary links must be re-derived too.
1109	        desynced = False
1110	        # Per-tenant tripwire: earliest global index at which a tenant has a
1111	        # record in a content-hash-failed window. Acts on tenants whose own
1112	        # chain nevertheless re-derives (a recomputed-digest forgery).
1113	        suspect: dict[str, int] = {}
1114	
1115	        for unit in units:
1116	            name = unit["name"]
1117	            path = unit["path"]
1118	            try:
1119	                stat = os.stat(path)
1120	            except FileNotFoundError:
1121	                if name == _FILE_UNIT:
1122	                    # The legacy file does not exist before the first append.
1123	                    continue
1124	                raise
1125	            entry = cached.get(name)
1126	            entry_fold = entry.get("fold") if entry is not None else None
1127	
1128	            if (
1129	                entry is not None
1130	                and entry_fold is not None
1131	                and not desynced
1132	                and self._entry_fresh(entry, stat, unit)
1133	            ):
1134	                self._adopt_states(states, entry)
1135	                total_records = entry["records"]
1136	                entries[name] = _cache_entry(
1137	                    total_records, stat, entry["parts"], states, entry_fold
1138	                )
1139	                continue
1140	
1141	            growth = (
1142	                entry is not None
1143	                and entry_fold is not None
1144	                and not desynced
1145	                and not unit["sealed"]
1146	                and stat.st_size > entry["size"]
1147	                and entry.get("parts", []) == unit["parts"]
1148	            )
1149	            if growth:
1150	                # Appended-only growth on the active unit. Before the
1151	                # cache's cumulative states are continued, the bytes the
1152	                # cache was built on authenticate themselves byte for byte:
1153	                # a fold over every complete line up to the cached size
1154	                # must equal the fold stored in the (tag-authenticated)
1155	                # cache. A rewritten prefix -- stale digests, recomputed
1156	                # digests, edited bytes behind preserved manifest windows,
1157	                # a shifted boundary -- changes that fold, so the
1158	                # continuation is refused and the walk falls through to a
1159	                # complete re-derivation, whose verdict equals a full
1160	                # verification and whose first bad index is the real
1161	                # position rather than the first new line.
1162	                with open(path, "rb") as handle:
1163	                    raw = handle.read()
1164	                prefix_raw = raw[: entry["size"]]
1165	                tail_raw = raw[entry["size"] :]
1166	                prefix_lines = _split_whole_lines(prefix_raw)
1167	                tail_lines = _split_whole_lines(tail_raw)
1168	                prefix_ok = (
1169	                    prefix_lines is not None
1170	                    and _fold_lines(prefix_lines) == entry_fold
1171	                )
1172	                if prefix_ok and tail_lines is not None:
1173	                    candidate = {
1174	                        tenant: list(state)
1175	                        for tenant, state in states.items()
1176	                    }
1177	                    self._adopt_states(candidate, entry)
1178	                    before_bad = {
1179	                        tenant: state[2] for tenant, state in candidate.items()
1180	                    }
1181	                    tail_records = st.decode_records(b"".join(tail_lines))
1182	                    self._apply_records(tail_records, candidate)
1183	                    tail_broken = any(
1184	                        state[2] != before_bad.get(tenant, -1)
1185	                        for tenant, state in candidate.items()
1186	                    )
1187	                    if not tail_broken:
1188	                        states.clear()
1189	                        states.update(candidate)
1190	                        total_records = entry["records"] + len(tail_records)
1191	                        new_fold = _extend_fold(entry_fold, tail_lines)
1192	                        entries[name] = _cache_entry(
1193	                            total_records,
1194	                            stat,
1195	                            entry.get("parts", []),
1196	                            states,
1197	                            new_fold,
1198	                        )
1199	                        continue
1200	                # Prefix authentication failed or the boundary moved:
1201	                # re-derive this unit completely below.
1202	
1203	            # Cold unit, shrink, same-size rewrite, any change to a sealed
1204	            # unit, a unit following one that desynced, or a growth whose
1205	            # cached prefix failed authentication: full parse; sealed windows
1206	            # are re-authenticated and every link is re-derived.
1207	            desynced = True
1208	            walked, parts, failed_tenants, fold = self._walk_bytes(unit, states)
1209	            for tenant, index in failed_tenants.items():
1210	                suspect.setdefault(tenant, index)
1211	            if entry is not None:
1212	                # The surviving cache anchors what this unit's per-tenant
1213	                # heads and counts must be. Legitimate writes take the
1214	                # growth branch above (or drop the cache via recover), so a
1215	                # stat change landing here whose re-derived heads differ is
1216	                # a rewritten history even when its digests recompute.
1217	                for tenant, anchored in entry["tenants"].items():
1218	                    current = states.get(tenant)
1219	                    if current is None:
1220	                        suspect.setdefault(tenant, 0)
1221	                    elif (
1222	                        current[0] != anchored[0] or current[1] != anchored[1]
1223	                    ) and current[2] == -1:
1224	                        suspect.setdefault(tenant, 0)
1225	                if stat.st_size < entry["size"]:
1226	                    # Records were deleted while the cache survived: flag the
1227	                    # first missing global index for each affected tenant.
1228	                    for tenant, anchored in entry["tenants"].items():
1229	                        current = states.get(tenant)
1230	                        remaining = current[0] if current is not None else 0
1231	                        if remaining < anchored[0]:
1232	                            suspect.setdefault(tenant, remaining)
1233	            total_records += walked
1234	            entries[name] = _cache_entry(total_records, stat, parts, states, fold)
1235	
1236	        # A chain break attributes first_bad precisely and is used as-is.
1237	        # Separately, every tenant with a record in a content-hash-failed
1238	        # window whose own chain still re-derives is flagged: its bytes were
1239	        # rewritten with recomputed digests and must not pass. This is
1240	        # evaluated per tenant, so a real break in another tenant's chain
1241	        # never suppresses it.
1242	        for tenant, index in suspect.items():
1243	            state = states.get(tenant)
1244	            if state is not None and state[2] == -1:
1245	                state[2] = index
1246	
1247	        # Never warm the cache from a walk that saw corruption: otherwise a
1248	        # manifest whose window anchors were rewritten would, on a second
1249	        # verify, match its own (bad) cached parts and take the constant hot
1250	        # path straight to a false pass. A corrupt tree is re-derived from
1251	        # bytes on every verify until it is genuinely repaired.
1252	        any_bad = any(state[2] != -1 for state in states.values())
1253	        if persist and not suspect and not any_bad:
1254	            st.save_cache(layout, entries)
1255	        return (
1256	            {tenant: (state[0], state[1], state[2]) for tenant, state in states.items()},
1257	            entries,
1258	        )

1260	    @staticmethod
1261	    def _adopt_states(states: dict[str, list], entry: dict) -> None:
1262	        for tenant, state in entry["tenants"].items():
1263	            count, digest, bad = state
1264	            current = states.get(tenant)
1265	            if current is None:
1266	                states[tenant] = [count, digest, bad]
1267	            else:
1268	                # Never let a cached -1 erase an earlier first_bad.
1269	                prior_bad = current[2]
1270	                if prior_bad != -1 and (bad == -1 or prior_bad < bad):
1271	                    bad = prior_bad
1272	                states[tenant] = [count, digest, bad]

1274	    @staticmethod
1275	    def _stat_fresh(entry: dict, stat: os.stat_result, *, exact: bool = True) -> bool:
1276	        # size + mtime identify an unchanged append-only file; ctime (which
1277	        # utimes cannot restore) exposes a same-size content rewrite. The
1278	        # growth branch only needs size-growth + unchanged ctime.
1279	        if entry["ctime_ns"] != stat.st_ctime_ns:
1280	            return False
1281	        if not exact:
1282	            return entry["size"] <= stat.st_size
1283	        return (
1284	            entry["size"] == stat.st_size
1285	            and entry["mtime_ns"] == stat.st_mtime_ns
1286	        )

1288	    @staticmethod
1289	    def _entry_fresh(entry: dict, stat: os.stat_result, unit: dict) -> bool:
1290	        """Hot-path freshness with constant read amplification.
1291	
1292	        The size + mtime + ctime guard identifies an unchanged append-only
1293	        file (ctime exposes a same-size content rewrite and cannot be
1294	        restored). In addition, whenever the unit carries preserved byte
1295	        windows -- always for a sealed unit, and for an active unit after a
1296	        fold-to-one compaction -- the manifest's window material must match
1297	        what the cache authenticated, so an edited manifest window forces
1298	        the cold path and is reported as corruption, without a single sealed
1299	        byte being hashed on the ordinary path.
1300	        """
1301	        if not Chain._stat_fresh(entry, stat):
1302	            return False
1303	        cached_parts = entry.get("parts", [])
1304	        if unit["sealed"] or cached_parts or unit["parts"]:
1305	            return cached_parts == unit["parts"]
1306	        return True

1308	    def _walk_bytes(
1309	        self, unit: dict, states: dict[str, list]
1310	    ) -> tuple[int, list[dict], dict, str]:
1311	        """Parse and chain one unit's bytes.
1312	
1313	        Returns ``(record_count, cache_parts, failed_tenants, fold)`` where
1314	        ``failed_tenants`` maps each tenant with a record in a
1315	        content-hash-failed window to that record's global index, and
1316	        ``fold`` is the extendable byte fingerprint of the unit's complete
1317	        lines.
1318	
1319	        Content tampering normally breaks the victim's digest chain, which
1320	        attributes ``first_bad`` precisely and leaves tenants with no record
1321	        in the damaged window untouched. The window hash is an independent
1322	        tripwire: it only needs to act when the attacker also recomputed
1323	        digests (a clean-looking but rewritten log).
1324	        """
1325	        path = unit["path"]
1326	        windows = unit["parts"]
1327	        with open(path, "rb") as handle:
1328	            raw = handle.read()
1329	
1330	        failed: set[int] = set()
1331	        window_ends: list[int] = []
1332	        if windows:
1333	            if unit["sealed"] and len(raw) != sum(
1334	                window["size"] for window in windows
1335	            ):
1336	                failed.update(range(len(windows)))
1337	            elif not st.verify_prefix_windows(path, windows):
1338	                failed.update(range(len(windows)))
1339	            running = 0
1340	            for window in windows:
1341	                running += window["size"]
1342	                window_ends.append(running)
1343	
1344	        try:
1345	            text = raw.decode(_ENCODING)
1346	        except UnicodeDecodeError as exc:
1347	            raise ValueError("malformed audit record") from exc
1348	        lines = rec.split_records(text)
1349	
1350	        first_index: dict[str, int] = {}
1351	        win_index = 0
1352	        pos = 0
1353	        for line in lines:
1354	            length = len((line + "\n").encode(_ENCODING))
1355	            start, end = pos, pos + length
1356	            pos = end
1357	            while win_index < len(window_ends) and start >= window_ends[win_index]:
1358	                win_index += 1
1359	            past_end = win_index >= len(window_ends)
1360	            crosses = not past_end and end > window_ends[win_index]
1361	            window_failed = not past_end and win_index in failed
1362	
1363	            record = rec.parse_line(line)
1364	            tenant = record["tenant"]
1365	            count, head, bad = states.get(tenant, [0, "", -1])
1366	            if window_failed:
1367	                first_index.setdefault(tenant, count)
1368	            if crosses:
1369	                # Windows only ever concatenate whole lines, so a record may
1370	                # never straddle a window boundary.
1371	                if bad == -1:
1372	                    bad = count
1373	            if unit["sealed"] and past_end and bad == -1:
1374	                # Bytes appended past a sealed segment's frozen material.
1375	                bad = count
1376	            recomputed = rec.digest(record["prev"], record["payload"])
1377	            if record["prev"] != head or record["digest"] != recomputed:
1378	                if bad == -1:
1379	                    bad = count
1380	            states[tenant] = [count + 1, record["digest"], bad]
1381	
1382	        # Sealed units carry their full window material; an active unit
1383	        # carries preserved *prefix* windows after a fold-to-one compaction.
1384	        # Both are retained in the cache so the hot-path freshness guard
1385	        # compares the manifest's window material for either kind.
1386	        parts = [dict(part) for part in windows]
1387	        # split_records guaranteed raw ends in a terminator, so this folds
1388	        # every complete line exactly as the continuation branch will.
1389	        fold = _fold_of_bytes(raw)
1390	        return len(lines), parts, first_index, fold

1392	    def _apply_records(self, records: list[dict], states: dict[str,list]) -> None:
1393	        for record in records:
1394	            tenant = record["tenant"]
1395	            count, head, bad = states.get(tenant, [0, "", -1])
1396	            recomputed = rec.digest(record["prev"], record["payload"])
1397	            if record["prev"] != head or record["digest"] != recomputed:
1398	                if bad == -1:
1399	                    bad = count
1400	            states[tenant] = [count + 1, record["digest"], bad]

1406	    def export_range(self, tenant: str, start: int, end: int) -> dict:
1407	        """Build an offline proof for tenant records ``[start, end)``.
1408	
1409	        The proof contains only the interval's chained records and the
1410	        window anchors (ordered, strictly increasing windows) needed to
1411	        attach the interval to the prefix and confirm it is contiguous. No
1412	        payload outside the interval is included. An independent reader can
1413	        check it with :func:`audit_chain.proof.verify_proof` and the public
1414	        digest function alone.
1415	
1416	        Illegal, reversed, empty or out-of-range intervals raise
1417	        ``ValueError``; for a tenant with no history the empty-history
1418	        conclusion ``(0, 0)`` is the only interval accepted.
1419	        """
1420	        from . import proof as pf
1421	
1422	        if (
1423	            not isinstance(start, int)
1424	            or not isinstance(end, int)
1425	            or isinstance(start, bool)
1426	            or isinstance(end, bool)
1427	        ):
1428	            raise ValueError("range bounds must be integers")
1429	        if start < 0 or end < 0:
1430	            raise ValueError("range bounds must be non-negative")
1431	        if end < start:
1432	            raise ValueError("range is reversed: start must be <= end")
1433	
1434	        with self._locked(exclusive=False) as layout:
1435	            if layout.kind == "file" and not os.path.exists(layout.root):
1436	                # A log that was never created implies an empty history for
1437	                # every tenant; only the (0, 0) empty-history conclusion is
1438	                # in bounds.
1439	                if (start, end) == (0, 0):
1440	                    return pf.empty_proof(tenant)
1441	                raise ValueError("range is out of bounds for an empty history")
1442	            units = self._snapshot_units(layout, tolerate_metadata=True)
1443	            # Fast path: an authentic warm cache states each unit's
1444	            # cumulative tenant counts, so only units holding interval bytes
1445	            # are opened. With no trustworthy guide (never-verified log,
1446	            # grown active unit, edited bytes or metadata) fall back to the
1447	            # full ordered byte scan.
1448	            guide = self._export_guide(units, layout, tenant)
1449	            if guide is not None:
1450	                material = self._collect_range_bounded(
1451	                    units, tenant, start, end, guide
1452	                )
1453	            else:
1454	                material = self._collect_range(units, tenant, start, end)
1455	        return pf.build_proof(material)

1469	    def _collect_range(
1470	        self, units: list[dict], tenant: str, start: int, end: int
1471	    ) -> dict:
1472	        """One ordered snapshot scan collecting interval material.
1473	
1474	        Windows are numbered with one strictly increasing global sequence
1475	        across all units, so the proof carries an explicit cross-segment
1476	        window chain. Only records of ``tenant`` are parsed; malformed lines
1477	        and a trailing half line outside the interval are skipped, so damage
